title: Mavinject process injection command
description: Detects Mavinject commands carrying a bounded INJECTRUNNING or HMODULE switch, including renamed executables identified by original-filename metadata. Successful injection and trustworthy binary identity require separate validation.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may abuse the signed Microsoft Mavinject utility to inject a DLL into another process.
hypothesis.rationale: Mavinject INJECTRUNNING and HMODULE switches can request process injection. Filename or original-filename metadata identifies a candidate binary but is spoofable; target-process and module telemetry are needed to confirm execution.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify Mavinject and renamed Mavinject executions that request INJECTRUNNING or HMODULE injection while leaving invocations without an injection switch, unrelated binaries and incomplete events unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Treat a selected Mavinject injection command as high-priority, then determine whether an approved Microsoft App-V or controlled security workflow explains it.
steps: Confirm the command's result in follow-on process, file, registry or service telemetry; a process-start event records intent and does not prove successful execution.
Review the complete command, target process identifier, DLL or module path, original filename, parent process, account and endpoint role.
Inspect the injected module and target process, then correlate file creation, signer, hash, network activity and follow-on behavior.
Confirm an approved App-V or security-testing workflow with its owner; otherwise contain the endpoint and investigate the payload source and process ancestry.
false_positives: Legitimate Microsoft App-V activity or explicitly authorized security testing that invokes Mavinject injection functionality

validation.expected_outcome: Match Mavinject or renamed Mavinject commands using INJECTRUNNING or HMODULE; do not match help or ordinary invocations, unrelated processes or missing command lines.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
